title: Light and How We See
seo_title: Grade 4 Light Worksheets: How We See Objects, Reflection and Light Sources
standard_text: Develop a model to describe that light reflecting from objects and entering the eye allows objects to be seen.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on light and how we see (NGSS 4-PS4-2): light reflecting off objects into the eye, light sources and reflectors, mirrors, the moon and light path models. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: We see things when light reflects off them into our eyes.
key_sub: Light goes from a source, like the sun or a lamp, to an object, and then bounces into our eyes. Eyes do not send out light.
body_html:
How to think about it

We see an object when light reflects (bounces) off it and enters our eyes. Light comes from a source, like the sun or a lamp. Our eyes do not send out light.

Most things, like books, walls and the moon, do not make their own light. We see them because they reflect light. Smooth, shiny surfaces like mirrors reflect light very well. In total darkness we cannot see anything, because no light can reach our eyes.

Example

How do you see a book on your desk?

The lamp or sun lights the book.

Light reflects off the book.

The light enters your eyes.

Answer: light source → book → eye

Example

Why can we see the moon?

The moon does not make light.

It reflects sunlight.

Answer: Sunlight reflects off the moon into our eyes.

Common mistakes

  • Drawing arrows from the eye to the object. Light goes into the eye.
  • Thinking the moon makes its own light.
  • Thinking eyes can see in total darkness after they adjust.

faq.a: Light from a source like the sun or a lamp reflects off the object and enters our eyes.

faq.q: Does the moon make its own light?
faq.a: No. The moon reflects sunlight. That is why the lit part of the moon always faces the sun.

faq.q: Can you see in total darkness?
faq.a: No. Without light, no light can reflect off objects into your eyes.

items.q: Why can we see the moon at night?
c: The moon makes its own light.
Sunlight reflects off the moon and travels to our eyes.
Street lights shine on the moon.
Our eyes light up the moon.
items.e: The moon is not a light source. It reflects light from the sun.

items.q: Which surface reflects light best?
c: a smooth mirror
a pile of dirt
a black rug
a dark sweater
items.e: Smooth, shiny surfaces reflect most light.

items.e: Light goes from the lamp to the object, bounces off (reflects) and enters the eye. Diagram C shows light coming out of the eye, which is wrong.

items.q: In which direction does light travel?
c: only in circles
it does not move

only up

Yes. Light goes from the lamp to the object and reflects into the eye.

c: Yes, always.

items.q: Ruby and a toy car are in a closet with the door shut. There is no light at all. Can she see the toy car?
